summary: A st-test pool tree has one writer: a free slot whose tree still has a process from a run that lost it is skipped until the process ends, and an index.lock left by a run killed mid-checkout is removed (and logged) only when no process is left, so the next run checks out instead of failing

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Runs re-execute main's st-test, so this applies to every run once it is on main. Without /proc (not Linux) no process can be seen, and a pool tree is taken as before.

manual.detail: No operator actions; a stale index.lock in a pool tree no longer needs removing by hand.
